text:
maria: Customer (FinServX) flagged BYO-KMS for the POC. They want CloudHSM-backed CMKs, 30-day rotation, audit certs, and clarification on latency and pricing. Also a security questionnaire is blocking the SOW. @aaron @jessica can you advise?

aaron: Quick summary: we support BYO-KMS via customer CloudHSM or KMS with HSM-backed CMKs. For a POC we can do either ephemeral KEK wrapping or full BYO depending on the SOW. Latency impact for remote KMS calls is typically ~2-6ms extra per request (region/proxy dependent).

jessica: They also asked for a key custody diagram, rotation cadence doc, and HSM attestation certs. I can pull our standard diagram. @maria can you drop the sec questionnaire link?

maria: Link: https://cust.example.com/sec-qa.pdf. They asked for dual-custody for cutover and confirmation we don’t retain plaintext keys. Pricing ask: dev POC (3 months) + staging with a dedicated HSM — they want a discount for BYO.

aaron: Dual custody: supported via multi-custodian key wrap patterns. For POC we can simulate with two HSMs or recommend BYO with two admins. For latency/cost guidance I'll give a short note. Tagging @ben for pricing.

ben: For SOW/ops we need network diagram + firewall rules. CloudHSM path: outbound to KMS endpoints over TCP 443 and NTP. On-prem HSM: our keyproxy needs 1500/tcp open. Runbook snippet: ```yaml
firewall:
  - 443/tcp
  - 1500/tcp
  - 123/udp
```

jessica: They requested rotation at 01:00 UTC and zero-downtime swaps. We support staged roll with wrap/unwrap and a fallback policy. Customer must provide a rotation-role API credential for acceptance tests. Example regen script for tests: ```bash
./rotate_keys.sh --env staging
```

maria: Can we offer reduced pricing if they provide the HSM AND perform local key wrapping? They want cost-savings vs us hosting keys.

ben: Yes — we can discount up to 20% on dedicated monthly charges if BYO-HSM reduces our operational footprint by >=90%. Legal needs a "customer-managed key addendum" signed. Looping in @elena.

elena: I’ll draft the addendum. Clarifying Q for the security doc: do we ever log plaintext keys? Answer: no — we only persist key references/metadata and audit events, never key material. I’ll add explicit language and attestation cert references.

maria: :thumbsup: Next steps: jessica to provide sec diagram + runbook snippet, ben to produce dev-pricing draft, elena to prepare addendum draft, aaron to confirm latency numbers with infra. Target internal POC kickoff next Tue — everyone able?

aaron: Works for me.

ben: SGTM.

jessica: I’ll drop artifacts by EOD.

maria: Thanks all :pray:
